data.name: Ayanyak
data.gender_notes: Ayanyak is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ayanyak is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Aya' meaning 'lord' and 'Nyak' meaning 'sacred' or 'pure'. This name is used to denote someone who is the lord or protector of the sacred. In Hindu mythology, Ayanyak is an epithet for various deities, particularly Lord Vishnu and Lord Ganesha, who are revered as the protectors of the dharma or righteous path.
data.spiritual_meaning: Protector of the sacred and dharma.
data.etymology: Ayanyak belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Sacred.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayanyak total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Ayanyak is a revered and respected name rooted deeply in the Hindu culture. The name signifies divine protection and carries the essence of strength and purity. Ayanyak is often used as a title for deities, gurus, or spiritual guides, and represents the lordly power and authority that comes with the role of a protector. In Hindu rituals and ceremonies, the invocation of Ayanyak is common as a means to seek divine protection and blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: Ayanyak represents the divine protector or guardian, who is believed to be the embodiment of pure consciousness and selfless service. The name resonates with the idea that the divine power is always watching over us and protecting us from harm. At a spiritual level, the name Ayanyak invokes a deep sense of trust and surrender to the higher power, instilling a feeling of peace and safety. It serves as a reminder of our inherent divine connection and the protection that comes with it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ayanyak signifies the embodiment of fearlessness and the divine protector. It is believed that one named Ayanyak is blessed with inner courage, strength, and the ability to shield themselves and others from harm.

historical_references.reference: Ayanyak, also known as Yayati, was a legendary king in Hindu mythology, the father of the Pandavas and the ancestor of the Kurus. He is said to have ruled around 3219 BCE.
historical_references.context: Legendary king and ancestor of the Kurus and Pandavas.

historical_references.reference: Ayanyak, or Yayati, is also mentioned in the Mahabharata as a powerful king who renounced his kingdom and underwent the curse of age, living out his remaining years as a wandering ascetic. This occurred around 3136 BCE.
historical_references.context: Renounced his kingdom and lived out his remaining years as a wandering ascetic.
